# Exercise 02-2

## Doing a simple calculation

The data set :

```{r}
data <- c(
  14.0, 7.6, 11.2, 12.8, 12.5, 9.9, 14.9, 9.4, 16.9, 10.2,
  14.9, 18.1, 7.3, 9.8, 10.9, 12.2, 9.9, 2.9, 2.8, 15.4,
  15.7, 9.7, 13.1, 13.2, 12.3, 11.7, 16.0, 12.4, 17.9, 12.2,
  16.2, 18.7, 8.9, 11.9, 12.1, 14.6, 12.1, 4.7, 3.9, 16.9,
  16.8, 11.3, 14.4, 15.7, 14.0, 13.6, 18.0, 13.6, 19.9, 13.7,
  17.0, 20.5, 9.9, 12.5, 13.2, 16.1, 13.5, 6.3, 6.4, 17.6,
  19.1, 12.8, 15.5, 16.3, 15.2, 14.6, 19.1, 14.4, 21.4, 15.1,
  19.6, 21.7, 11.3, 15.0, 14.3, 16.8, 14.0, 6.8, 8.2, 19.9,
  20.4, 14.6, 16.4, 18.7, 16.8, 15.8, 20.4, 15.8, 22.4, 16.2,
  20.3, 23.4, 12.1, 15.5, 15.4, 18.4, 15.7, 10.2, 8.9, 21.0
)
data
```

The mean

```{r}
mean(data)
```

The standard deviation

```{r}
sd(data)
```

The minimum

```{r}
min(data)
```

The media
```{r}
median(data)
```


The maximum
```{r}
max(data)
```



```{r}
summary(data)
```

```{r, include=FALSE}
# c(...)    : "combine", builds a vector (the data set) from the values
#
# mean()   : average of all values
# sd()     : standard deviation (spread around the mean)
# min()    : smallest value
# median() : middle value (half the values are below, half above)
# max()    : largest value
# summary(): prints min, 1st quartile, median, mean, 3rd quartile and max
#
```

# Exercise 02-3

## Plotting the data

Sequence plot (each value in the order it appears) :

```{r}
plot(data,
     type = "l",
     col = "blue",
     main = "Data in sequence",
     xlab = "Index",
     ylab = "Value")
grid()
```

Histogram of the data :

```{r}
hist(data,
     col = "blue",
     main = "Histogram of the data",
     xlab = "Value",
     ylab = "Frequency")
grid()
```

```{r, include=FALSE}
# plot(data) : plots the values against their position (1, 2, 3, ...)
#   type = "p" points, "l" lines, "b" both points and lines
# hist(data) : draws a histogram
#   breaks = number of intervals ("bins") on the x-axis
#
# Common arguments for both:
#   col  = colour of the points/bars ("blue", "orange", "#FF8800", ...)
#   main = title above the graph
#   xlab = label under the x-axis
#   ylab = label next to the y-axis
```
